cards.title: === compares
cards.body: `===` is true when two values are exactly the same, type included. `!==` means "not equal".

cards.title: Why not ==
cards.body: `==` converts types before comparing, so `"1" == 1` is true. That causes surprises, so use `===`.

cards.title: Spot the bug
cards.body: Whatever colour you type, it always says `My favourite too!`. Tap the bug.

bug.fix: `=` stores `"blue"` in `color`, so the condition is always true. Compare with `===`: `if (color === "blue")`.

check.question: What does this print?
check.explanation: One is a number and the other is text, so `===` says they are not the same.
